subtopic: Tree and Graph Traversals (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra, A*)
question_text: In Kahn's algorithm for Topological Sorting on a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), what is the graph invariant maintained by the in-degree array?

options.text: Nodes with zero in-degree have no remaining unvisited prerequisite dependencies
Nodes with maximum in-degree are processed first to maximize parallelism
The in-degree tracks the shortest distance from the source
In-degree is decremented only when back edges are encountered

answer_explanation: Kahn's algorithm operates by repeatedly picking vertices with an in-degree of 0, meaning all prerequisite dependencies have been met and emitted. Emitting a node decrements the in-degrees of its immediate neighbors.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Kahn's algorithm operates by repeatedly picking vertices with an in-degree of 0, meaning all prerequisite dependencies have been met and emitted. Emitting a node decrements the in-degrees of its immediate neighbors.

criteria.name: Correctness
criteria.description: Selects the exact correct technical option.
